subject.title: [Feature]: Capability-based permissions for skills/tools (default-deny high-risk actions)

question: What public capability taxonomy, grant storage, default-deny upgrade behavior, and enforcement boundary should OpenClaw adopt for skills/tools?
rationale: The item defines public plugin/skill metadata, persisted grants, security semantics, and upgrade behavior that cannot be safely inferred from the current adjacent name-based policies.

options.title: Approve phased core capability model
options.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics and design the grant, enforcement, and audit layers behind a maintainer-approved contract before default-deny enforcement ships.

options.title: Limit this to manifest descriptors
options.body: Keep enforcement in existing tool-policy and hook surfaces while adding only visible capability declarations for inspection and later RFC work.

options.title: Keep governance plugin-only
options.body: Close or narrow the core item if maintainers decide current hooks and plugins are the intended boundary for this class of policy.

recommendation.title: Approve phased core capability model
recommendation.body: Start with schema/parser diagnostics and design the grant, enforcement, and audit layers behind a maintainer-approved contract before default-deny enforcement ships.

likelyOwner.reason: Security and gateway enforcement boundaries are the main unresolved product decision surface, and recent history links this owner to adjacent policy work and discussion.
